mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL over the prior quarter indicates a restrictive monetary policy with falling inflation, which typically supports equity valuations through stable real rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls in the same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month averages signals a synchronized expansion in income and housing demand, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both above 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) signals improved labor supply without rising unemployment, which boosts productivity and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable and PAYEMS rising q/q for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of the macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
